bulk-links.title: Create links in bulk
bulk-links.markdown:
# Create links in bulk

`POST /v1/links/bulk` accepts a JSON object with a `links` array of 1–1,000
link creation inputs. The entire request body must fit within 1 MiB. Use a key
with `links:write` whose creator can create resources in the workspace.
Each row supports the same destination, domain, key, title, description, tags and
password options, validation and plan gates as `POST /v1/links`.

```sh
curl https://api.shortn.at/v1/links/bulk \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SHORTN_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Idempotency-Key: campaign-launch-001' \
  --data '{"links":[{"url":"https://example.com/first","tags":["Launch"]},{"url":"https://example.com/second","tags":["Launch"]}]}'
```

## Results and atomicity

A successful request returns HTTP 201 with `count` and `items` in the input order.
Each item has the same shape as a newly created individual link. Destination
safety starts pending, with a durable background scan request committed alongside
each link. The worker scans new destinations and retries failures; configured
safety and password gates still apply at redirect time. If there are enabled
subscribers, each link produces its own `link.created` event.

The batch commits in one Mongo transaction. Invalid input, taken or duplicate
keys, a missing plan feature, insufficient quota, or a database/event write failure
creates no batch links or new tags. A workspace quota check covers the entire
batch and is serialized with other v2 link and QR backing-link creation requests.
Keys are checked again inside the transaction; database uniqueness handles racing
inserts. Foreign-workspace tags are never reused, including when legacy owner
fields happen to match.

Errors use `application/problem+json`. Validation or key errors may include a
`context.index` identifying the zero-based input row. HTTP 409 `limit_reached`
includes `context.limit`, `context.used` and `context.requested` so the integration
can show the exact remaining capacity. A validation failure in the request envelope
returns HTTP 400; an oversized body returns HTTP 413.

## Retries

Send a unique `Idempotency-Key` for each intended batch and retain it for retries.
The original status and response are retained for 24 hours. Reusing the key with a
different request returns HTTP 409 `idempotency_conflict`. An uncertain in-flight
operation returns `idempotency_pending`; it is not reissued automatically.
Feature flags, membership, role and scopes are checked before replaying a response.

This endpoint creates a bounded batch. CSV upload, mapping, dry runs, whole-import
quota reservation and resumable background imports remain separate work.

The batch commits in one Mongo transaction. Invalid input, taken or duplicate keys, a missing plan feature, insufficient quota, or a database/event write failure creates no batch links or new tags. A workspace quota check covers the entire batch and is serialized with other v2 link and QR backing-link creation requests. Keys are checked again inside the transaction; database uniqueness handles racing inserts. Foreign-workspace tags are never reused, including when legacy owner fields happen to match.

Errors use application/problem+json. Validation or key errors may include a context.index identifying the zero-based input row. HTTP 409 limit_reached includes context.limit, context.used and context.requested so the integration can show the exact remaining capacity. A validation failure in the request envelope returns HTTP 400; an oversized body returns HTTP 413.

Retries

Send a unique Idempotency-Key for each intended batch and retain it for retries. The original status and response are retained for 24 hours. Reusing the key with a different request returns HTTP 409 idempotency_conflict. An uncertain in-flight operation returns idempotency_pending; it is not reissued automatically. Feature flags, membership, role and scopes are checked before replaying a response.

This endpoint creates a bounded batch. CSV upload, mapping, dry runs, whole-import quota reservation and resumable background imports remain separate work.

# Exports

The local backend supports incremental CSV/JSON encoding, the shared Links view
filters, Mongo snapshot cursors and durable private-object-store jobs. Private dashboard HTTP delivery and in-page review, progress and history are implemented locally. Analytics job encoding, workers and private HTTP delivery are also implemented locally; the analytics dashboard is connected locally; full-workspace archive jobs/private HTTP and ready-email outbox are implemented locally, with their dashboard and email sign-in return connected locally; this document does not claim complete P6 export coverage.

`EXPORTS_ENABLED` defaults to `0` in web, API and worker schemas. Enabled startup
requires `S3_ENDPOINT`, `S3_REGION`, `S3_BUCKET`, `S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and
`S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`; production uses HTTPS. Deploy the `export_jobs` indexes
and private 24-hour object lifecycle before enabling. The worker pumps bounded
pages of due jobs into BullMQ and closes its own queue clients on shutdown.

Core validates filter shapes and reads current membership and plan entitlement.
`csvExport` gates CSV and JSON; a campaign-scoped export also requires
`campaignExport`. Workspace/legacy ownership, hidden and QR exclusions, trash,
search, tags, campaign, status and date behavior come from the same filter helper
as Links browsing. The exported fields are destination URL, key, title, tag
names, domain, expiry, created time and click total. Password hashes, safety
internals, user identifiers and signing keys are never export columns.

For fewer than 5,000 rows, `prepareLinkExport` returns a **server-only** selection
of at most 4,999 IDs. Pass it to `streamFilteredLinkExport`; never send the
selection to the browser or use a client-side library fetch. The bounded IDs
prevent concurrent inserts/filter changes growing the instant response past the
threshold. A Mongo snapshot cursor streams batches of 500, preserving a stable
view through concurrent updates. Authorization and plan reads run outside that
snapshot on each batch; abort closes the cursor/session.

At 5,000 rows or more, preparation creates a 24-hour export job. A request UUID
deduplicates retries for the same workspace/creator/format/filter; changing the
request under that UUID conflicts. The worker streams a complete CSV or JSON
file to private storage with a one-GiB transport bound, renews the fenced lease,
updates processed-row counts and retries transient transport failures. Recovery
restarts encoding into a fresh attempt object. No partial object is signed.
Only an unexpired completed job's own `exports/jobs/links/{workspace}/{job}/`
object can be delivered. Results expire from job creation, and signed delivery
never extends the remaining lifetime. Cancellation or a replaced lease prevents
the obsolete worker from publishing. Creators and current workspace admins/owners
may inspect jobs; membership/plan access is checked again at delivery.

CSV declares `shortn_format=shortn-csv-v1`. Formula-looking values are protected
with an apostrophe and literal apostrophes doubled; the importer reverses this
only for declared Shortn rows. Tags use JSON arrays within CSV cells so embedded
commas/semicolons remain lossless. The URL remains complete rather than splitting
UTM parameters, preserving duplicate parameters and fragments. Ordinary CSV
input keeps its previous behavior. Existing import file/row/field limits apply
to exported files being imported again.

Local integration evidence lives in `apps/worker/src/imports.integration.test.ts`:
actual worker round trip into a new workspace, 4,999/5,000 boundary, frozen instant
selection, snapshot consistency, abort/current membership and plan checks,
private signing/expiry, retry and idempotency, cancellation, stale-lease recovery,
and a real BullMQ queue. Parser/format tests cover formula safety and reversible
tags/quotes/apostrophes. All services in those tests are synthetic/loopback. Real
bucket CORS/signing/multipart/lifecycle and staging acceptance remain separate gates.

## Private dashboard HTTP delivery

These routes use the dashboard session cookie, not public API keys. All responses
are private/no-store with Cookie variance and nosniff. The independent web export
flag and current membership/plan access gate every operation.

| Route | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /api/link-exports/{workspace}` | Metadata-only preparation; returns 201 with a download URL for <5,000 selected rows or 202 with safe job metadata and a status URL for larger views. |
| `GET /api/link-exports/{workspace}/download/{ref}` | Authenticated attachment stream for the creator-bound frozen selection; no browser library payload. |
| `GET /api/link-exports/{workspace}/jobs/{id}` | Authenticated safe progress/terminal metadata, with private signed delivery only for a valid completed job. |
| `POST /api/link-exports/{workspace}/jobs/{id}` | `{ "action": "cancel" }`; repeated cancellation is idempotent, and completed/failed jobs return 409. |

Preparation accepts JSON `{ format: "csv" | "json", filter?: { ... }, requestId?:
UUID }`. Filter names match core search/tags/campaign/status/createdAfter/
createdBefore/trash/sort; dates accept ISO date-time strings. JSON bodies are
bounded to 32 KiB even without Content-Length. Unknown fields/operators,
malformed JSON and inappropriate content types fail before preparation.
Preparation/cancellation require an exact Origin matching the configured dashboard
origin; missing or foreign origins return 403. Authentication returns 401, missing
workspaces/tokens/jobs 404, absent export entitlement 403, idempotency conflicts
409, oversized metadata 413 and wrong content type 415.

Instant selections remain in durable Redis under a workspace/creator/ref key for
15 minutes. Responses contain only a ref URL, format, count and expiry; the
4,999-or-fewer IDs and complete filter never reach the browser. Downloads validate
the current session, token lifetime, membership and export entitlement again.
The pull-based response preserves backpressure and closes/aborts the cursor on
request abort or response cancellation. Attachments use fixed safe filenames.
HEAD requests perform the same access/token checks without opening a data cursor.
These private endpoints do not extend the public REST contract listed in spec 10.

`apps/web/e2e/link-exports-http.local.ts` runs against the loopback P6 sandbox and
owns a synthetic private object store and real BullMQ worker. It verifies an actual
4,999-row Chromium attachment, reversible CSV bytes, concurrent insertion without
selection growth, a 5,000-row queued JSON artifact, private response headers,
origin/body-shape boundaries, a valid foreign workspace, creator-bound token expiry,
request deduplication, cancellation/retry/completed-state behavior and current plan
revocation. Evidence is saved in `.impeccable/review/p6-link-export-http/evidence.json`.
Transport unit tests verify body bounds, exact origin matching, pull backpressure,
request abort and iterator cleanup. No external provider writes are involved.


## Dashboard review, progress and history

The Links header opens `/{workspace}/links/export` with the current search, tags,
status, created-date, trash and sort scope. Pagination and row selection do not
narrow this whole-filter export. The review shows the total and 25 rows per page,
grouped by creation date, using the Links controls and divided list styling.
Tag suggestions are capped at 50 and search on the server; selected names remain
available when suggestions change. The main Links page uses the same bounded
suggestions. No complete link library is fetched into the browser.

Choose CSV or JSON and prepare the export once. Small exports show a download
link valid for 15 minutes. Background exports open a status page with processed
counts, cancellation and private download on completion. Polling pauses while
the page is hidden and preserves retryable failures; invalid access removes any
signed download. History shows unexpired background jobs, 25 per page, with
status and format filters. Members/viewers see their own jobs; current workspace
admins/owners can inspect workspace jobs. Expired jobs and plan/access loss have
in-page recovery actions. The pages are translated into English, Portuguese and
Spanish and use the existing light/dark themes.

`apps/web/e2e/link-exports-ui.local.ts` verifies a synthetic 5,000-link/103-tag
library, filter preservation, whole-filter 27-row CSV/JSON downloads across two
review pages, duplicate-submit prevention, remote tag search outside the first
50 suggestions, empty state, cancellation, actual BullMQ worker delivery,
30-job history pagination/filtering, expiry, plan loss and 390px bounds. Captures
and assertions are in `.impeccable/review/p6-link-export-ui/evidence.json`.
This is local dashboard evidence; analytics/workspace exports and external
storage/staging acceptance remain open.


## Analytics export jobs

Analytics exports always use durable jobs: aggregate CSV, or raw CSV/NDJSON.
`POST /api/analytics-exports/{workspace}` accepts only metadata:

```json
{
  "requestId": "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001",
  "query": {
    "mode": "raw",
    "format": "ndjson",
    "scope": { "type": "workspace" },
    "from": "2026-10-01T00:00:00Z",
    "to": "2026-10-15T00:00:00Z",
    "timezone": "UTC",
    "interval": "day",
    "filters": {},
    "dimensions": []
  }
}
```

The response is 202 with safe job metadata and an API `statusUrl`.
`GET /api/analytics-exports/{workspace}/jobs/{id}` reads progress and completed
private delivery. POST to that job with `{ "action": "cancel" }` cancels a
pending/running job; cancellation retries succeed, while completed/failed jobs
return 409. GET the collection path for 25-row history, with `page`, `state`,
`format` and `mode` filters. These private dashboard routes use session cookies,
exact Origin checks on mutations, a 32 KiB metadata body bound and the same
private/no-store headers and current creator/admin visibility as link exports.
They are not public bearer-authenticated REST operations.

Owned link, QR, tag and campaign scopes and filter semantics share analytics
resolution. `csvExport` gates either format and `campaignExport` additionally
gates campaign scope. Preparation clamps the lower bound to the plan window and
the upper bound to request time. That effective window is retained during a plan
upgrade; current membership, scope and entitlement are rechecked outside the
snapshot during batches, worker heartbeats and delivery. A downgrade that narrows
the prepared window fails closed. Window age is anchored at request time, so
ordinary elapsed execution time does not continuously move the export's start.

Raw rows explicitly contain timestamp, event kind, key, country, city, continent,
device, browser, OS, referrer, language, branch and five UTM values. Event/tenant/
actor IDs, IP hashes, raw IP and user agents are excluded. NDJSON preserves the
original values; CSV protects spreadsheet formula prefixes. Raw cursors use
500-row batches. All sections of one aggregate file and raw traversal share a
Mongo snapshot session, including on the native time-series collection. Cursors
and sessions close on completion, failure and abort.

Aggregate CSV columns are `section,dimension,value,period,clicks,scans,uniques`.
It contains a total, populated time buckets in the requested timezone/interval,
and every group for each requested plan-allowed dimension. It does not inherit
the dashboard's top-row cap. Empty ranges include a zero total. Two-stage grouping
counts distinct visitors without building one unbounded visitor array; Mongo may
spill grouping to disk. Visitor hashes never appear in the file.

Analytics jobs use a separate kind and queue in the export collection; link
workers and endpoints explicitly exclude that kind. Due/history indexes include
kind. The fenced, renewable worker writes a unique attempt object below
`exports/jobs/analytics/{workspace}/{job}/`, with the existing one-GiB transport
bound, five transient retries and 24-hour lifecycle. Only a completed current
attempt is signed, for at most its remaining lifetime; cancellation or a replaced
lease prevents stale publication. Worker startup/pump/shutdown use the existing
independent `EXPORTS_ENABLED` flag, which remains off by default.

`apps/worker/src/analytics-exports.integration.test.ts` verifies native time-series
snapshot consistency, more than 1,000 aggregate groups, bounded raw traversal,
DTO redaction/formula safety, retention/plan changes, retries, cancellation,
replaced/expired leases, current roles, kind/tenant isolation, expiry, pagination
and a real BullMQ pump. `apps/web/e2e/analytics-exports-http.local.ts` verifies the
actual authenticated Next routes and 1,005-row private downloads in all three
mode/format combinations. Its synthetic evidence is in
`.impeccable/review/p6-analytics-export-backend/http-evidence.json`.
The analytics dashboard and breakdown pages now open in-page job review rather
than fetching an entire CSV response into browser memory. Full-workspace export, real storage/staging acceptance and
other P6 deliverables remain open.


## Analytics dashboard

Analytics and full-breakdown Export actions open `/{workspace}/analytics/export`,
preserving browser-local dates/timezone, interval, owned campaign scope, link/kind
and event filters. A breakdown entry retains that requested dimension. The page
shows the effective retained window, a current all-matching event count and
readable scope/filter values. It submits that bounded window, so a plan upgrade
before preparation cannot widen the reviewed range. The form offers aggregate
CSV and raw CSV/NDJSON; aggregate groups are disclosed only in aggregate mode.
Raw exports with no matching events are disabled; a valid empty aggregate view
can still export zero totals. Dates wholly outside retention have no prepare
action until the user changes the view.

Preparation opens in-page progress with written-row counts and indeterminate
activity, cancellation and a completed private download. Polling pauses while
hidden, uses one request at a time and removes delivery links on expired or lost
access. History filters mode/state/format on the server with 25-row pages.
The UI uses the shared Page, native selectors, divided rows, FilterBar and
Pagination with English, Portuguese and Spanish in both themes. It introduces
no library picker or complete browser library/event fetch. The older private
`/api/export/{workspace}` endpoint remains present for compatibility, but the
dashboard no longer calls it.

`apps/web/e2e/analytics-exports-ui.local.ts` exercises synthetic 5,000-link/101-tag
libraries with 1,005 matching events, all three mode/format downloads through a
real worker, breakdown entry, scope preservation, duplicate submits, cancellation,
30-job history pagination/filtering, empty/expired/plan states and 1440/390px
layouts. Evidence is in `.impeccable/review/p6-analytics-export-ui/evidence.json`.


## Full-workspace archive jobs

`POST /api/workspace-exports/{workspace}` accepts only an optional request UUID,
for example `{ "requestId": "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001" }`.
It returns 202 safe job metadata and an API status URL. GET the collection for
25-row history (`page`, `state`); GET `jobs/{id}` for status and completed private
delivery; POST `jobs/{id}` with `{ "action": "cancel" }` to cancel. The routes use
session cookies, exact mutation Origin checks, a 32 KiB metadata limit and
private/no-store headers. Completed/failed cancellation returns 409, cancellation
retries succeed, unknown/expired jobs return 404 and current-role refusal is 403.
These are private dashboard routes rather than public REST API operations.

Authorization requires both the current workspace owner ID and a current owner
membership; a stale session role is insufficient. This portability export has no
paid `csvExport` or analytics-window gate. A workspace may have **one active
archive**; a different request while it is pending/running returns 409
`export_in_progress`. A partial unique index enforces that limit across requests.
Accepted UUID retries return the original job. Expired active rows release the
slot before eventual TTL deletion. Install the new active/mail indexes before
enabling the worker. The one-GiB transport bound applies to the complete ZIP;
size failure never exposes a partial download.

The ZIP contains 18 fixed-name entries:

- `workspace.json` and versioned `manifest.json` with record counts.
- JSON and CSV for links, QR codes, bio pages, retained bio-page versions,
  campaigns, tags and domains.
- `analytics.json` and `analytics.csv`, containing aggregate totals, populated
  daily UTC buckets and every dimension over all stored canonical workspace
  events. No visitor hash or raw event payload is exported.

Native and legacy personal-workspace ownership follow the same core predicates
as browsing. Hidden, QR-backing and trashed links are included. Link JSON retains
rules, social preview, UTM and reference metadata; link CSV uses the existing
reversible `shortn-csv-v1` format. QR JSON/CSV preserves stored design options,
including legacy gradients. Bio exports retain normalized draft/published content,
versions and complete owned legacy link/configuration data, so editor migration
limits do not truncate the archive. Foreign link references are omitted.
Complex CSV cells contain JSON and spreadsheet formula prefixes are protected.
Images remain referenced by URL; binary images/QR render files are not bundled.
Auth/session records, password hashes, signing credentials, provider verification
secrets and raw visitor data are excluded through explicit DTOs/projections.

A single Mongo snapshot covers workspace metadata and every resource/aggregate
file. Cursors use 500-row batches and close with their session on EOF, failure or
abort. ZIP output drains after each source chunk, preserving storage backpressure
instead of accumulating a library/archive in memory. Current ownership is checked
outside the snapshot between batches and on the renewable fenced worker lease.
Cancellation, ownership loss, replaced leases and expiry prevent publication.
Retries use a fresh attempt object under
`exports/jobs/workspace/{workspace}/{job}/`; results and signatures never outlive
the job's 24 hours from request. Startup/pump/shutdown use `EXPORTS_ENABLED`, still
off by default, with the existing private S3 configuration and job lifecycle.

Ready email has a separate leased outbox in the job. Storage completion remains
available if mail fails; transport retries do not regenerate the ZIP. Sending
requires the requester to remain the current owner and have a current verified
auth-account email. Revoked ownership suppresses delivery. Localized en/pt/es
HTML/text uses the shared mail layout and a stable provider idempotency key.
The email points to an authenticated workspace export page, so forwarding an email
does not give a download capability. Current-owner access and expiry are checked
again before signing the file. Configure `APP_URL`, `RESEND_API_KEY`, `MAIL_FROM`
and the intended `MAIL_ALLOWLIST`; absent/unavailable mail transport leaves a
retryable pending notification. The ready link opens the authenticated job page;
signing in preserves the exact validated workspace-export destination. Incoming
headers cannot supply an alternate return path.

`apps/worker/src/workspace-exports.integration.test.ts` verifies a 5,001-link ZIP,
a 2,501-link legacy bio, all content categories, one cross-file snapshot during
writes, secret/tenant isolation, all stored aggregates on a free plan, owner
changes, concurrent active requests/expiry, running cancellation, retries and
stale leases, separate mail retry/idempotency and a real BullMQ pump.
`apps/web/e2e/workspace-exports-http.local.ts` verifies actual session HTTP and an
18-entry private S3 ZIP, metadata bounds, free-owner access, current-role refusal,
kind/tenant isolation, UUIDs, cancellation/history/expiry. Evidence is in
`.impeccable/review/p6-workspace-export-backend/http-evidence.json`.

### Workspace dashboard

The current owner sees Export workspace in General settings. The in-page review
at `/{workspace}/settings/workspace/export` explains archive scope, exclusions,
the 1 GiB limit, one-active-job limit and 24-hour expiry. A live job replaces
Prepare with Continue export. Submission uses a stable request UUID and a local
duplicate guard; no library rows are fetched into the browser.

`/{workspace}/settings/workspace/exports/{id}` shows truthful phase/row progress,
cancellation, expiry, private ZIP download and separate pending/sent/failed email
state. Polling pauses in hidden tabs and continues at a lower frequency for a
completed archive whose email is pending. A completed download remains available
while email retries; expired or unauthorized reads remove it. Manual actions
invalidate stale poll responses. History at `.../exports` uses shared filters,
divided list rows and server-side 25-row pagination.

`apps/web/e2e/workspace-exports-ui.local.ts` verifies an isolated free workspace
with 5,001 links, 100 tags and 2,501 legacy bio references, real BullMQ/private
synthetic S3 generation and download of all 18 ZIP entries, duplicate submission,
active-job continuation, cancellation, history pages/state filtering, retry,
owner loss and expiry. A fake notifier verifies pending-to-sent polling and the
signed-out email → sign-in → exact job → ZIP flow without real provider mail.
Desktop/mobile en/pt/es light/dark evidence and design review live in
`.impeccable/review/p6-workspace-export-ui/`. Helper tests reject external,
traversing and malformed return paths. Real email/R2/staging acceptance and
remaining P6 requirements stay open.

These private dashboard routes use session cookies, exact Origin checks on mutations, a 32 KiB metadata body bound and the same private/no-store headers and current creator/admin visibility as link exports. They are not public bearer-authenticated REST operations.

Owned link, QR, tag and campaign scopes and filter semantics share analytics resolution. csvExport gates either format and campaignExport additionally gates campaign scope. Preparation clamps the lower bound to the plan window and the upper bound to request time. That effective window is retained during a plan upgrade; current membership, scope and entitlement are rechecked outside the snapshot during batches, worker heartbeats and delivery. A downgrade that narrows the prepared window fails closed. Window age is anchored at request time, so ordinary elapsed execution time does not continuously move the export's start.

Raw rows explicitly contain timestamp, event kind, key, country, city, continent, device, browser, OS, referrer, language, branch and five UTM values. Event/tenant/ actor IDs, IP hashes, raw IP and user agents are excluded. NDJSON preserves the original values; CSV protects spreadsheet formula prefixes. Raw cursors use 500-row batches. All sections of one aggregate file and raw traversal share a Mongo snapshot session, including on the native time-series collection. Cursors and sessions close on completion, failure and abort.

Aggregate CSV columns are section,dimension,value,period,clicks,scans,uniques. It contains a total, populated time buckets in the requested timezone/interval, and every group for each requested plan-allowed dimension. It does not inherit the dashboard's top-row cap. Empty ranges include a zero total. Two-stage grouping counts distinct visitors without building one unbounded visitor array; Mongo may spill grouping to disk. Visitor hashes never appear in the file.

Analytics jobs use a separate kind and queue in the export collection; link workers and endpoints explicitly exclude that kind. Due/history indexes include kind. The fenced, renewable worker writes a unique attempt object below exports/jobs/analytics/{workspace}/{job}/, with the existing one-GiB transport bound, five transient retries and 24-hour lifecycle. Only a completed current attempt is signed, for at most its remaining lifetime; cancellation or a replaced lease prevents stale publication. Worker startup/pump/shutdown use the existing independent EXPORTS_ENABLED flag, which remains off by default.

apps/worker/src/analytics-exports.integration.test.ts verifies native time-series snapshot consistency, more than 1,000 aggregate groups, bounded raw traversal, DTO redaction/formula safety, retention/plan changes, retries, cancellation, replaced/expired leases, current roles, kind/tenant isolation, expiry, pagination and a real BullMQ pump. apps/web/e2e/analytics-exports-http.local.ts verifies the actual authenticated Next routes and 1,005-row private downloads in all three mode/format combinations. Its synthetic evidence is in .impeccable/review/p6-analytics-export-backend/http-evidence.json. The analytics dashboard and breakdown pages now open in-page job review rather than fetching an entire CSV response into browser memory. Full-workspace export, real storage/staging acceptance and other P6 deliverables remain open.

Analytics dashboard

Analytics and full-breakdown Export actions open /{workspace}/analytics/export, preserving browser-local dates/timezone, interval, owned campaign scope, link/kind and event filters. A breakdown entry retains that requested dimension. The page shows the effective retained window, a current all-matching event count and readable scope/filter values. It submits that bounded window, so a plan upgrade before preparation cannot widen the reviewed range. The form offers aggregate CSV and raw CSV/NDJSON; aggregate groups are disclosed only in aggregate mode. Raw exports with no matching events are disabled; a valid empty aggregate view can still export zero totals. Dates wholly outside retention have no prepare action until the user changes the view.

Preparation opens in-page progress with written-row counts and indeterminate activity, cancellation and a completed private download. Polling pauses while hidden, uses one request at a time and removes delivery links on expired or lost access. History filters mode/state/format on the server with 25-row pages. The UI uses the shared Page, native selectors, divided rows, FilterBar and Pagination with English, Portuguese and Spanish in both themes. It introduces no library picker or complete browser library/event fetch. The older private /api/export/{workspace} endpoint remains present for compatibility, but the dashboard no longer calls it.

apps/web/e2e/analytics-exports-ui.local.ts exercises synthetic 5,000-link/101-tag libraries with 1,005 matching events, all three mode/format downloads through a real worker, breakdown entry, scope preservation, duplicate submits, cancellation, 30-job history pagination/filtering, empty/expired/plan states and 1440/390px layouts. Evidence is in .impeccable/review/p6-analytics-export-ui/evidence.json.

Full-workspace archive jobs

POST /api/workspace-exports/{workspace} accepts only an optional request UUID, for example { "requestId": "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001" }. It returns 202 safe job metadata and an API status URL. GET the collection for 25-row history (page, state); GET jobs/{id} for status and completed private delivery; POST jobs/{id} with { "action": "cancel" } to cancel. The routes use session cookies, exact mutation Origin checks, a 32 KiB metadata limit and private/no-store headers. Completed/failed cancellation returns 409, cancellation retries succeed, unknown/expired jobs return 404 and current-role refusal is 403. These are private dashboard routes rather than public REST API operations.

Authorization requires both the current workspace owner ID and a current owner membership; a stale session role is insufficient. This portability export has no paid csvExport or analytics-window gate. A workspace may have one active archive; a different request while it is pending/running returns 409 export_in_progress. A partial unique index enforces that limit across requests. Accepted UUID retries return the original job. Expired active rows release the slot before eventual TTL deletion. Install the new active/mail indexes before enabling the worker. The one-GiB transport bound applies to the complete ZIP; size failure never exposes a partial download.

The ZIP contains 18 fixed-name entries:

  • workspace.json and versioned manifest.json with record counts.
  • JSON and CSV for links, QR codes, bio pages, retained bio-page versions, campaigns, tags and domains.
  • analytics.json and analytics.csv, containing aggregate totals, populated daily UTC buckets and every dimension over all stored canonical workspace events. No visitor hash or raw event payload is exported.

Native and legacy personal-workspace ownership follow the same core predicates as browsing. Hidden, QR-backing and trashed links are included. Link JSON retains rules, social preview, UTM and reference metadata; link CSV uses the existing reversible shortn-csv-v1 format. QR JSON/CSV preserves stored design options, including legacy gradients. Bio exports retain normalized draft/published content, versions and complete owned legacy link/configuration data, so editor migration limits do not truncate the archive. Foreign link references are omitted. Complex CSV cells contain JSON and spreadsheet formula prefixes are protected. Images remain referenced by URL; binary images/QR render files are not bundled. Auth/session records, password hashes, signing credentials, provider verification secrets and raw visitor data are excluded through explicit DTOs/projections.

A single Mongo snapshot covers workspace metadata and every resource/aggregate file. Cursors use 500-row batches and close with their session on EOF, failure or abort. ZIP output drains after each source chunk, preserving storage backpressure instead of accumulating a library/archive in memory. Current ownership is checked outside the snapshot between batches and on the renewable fenced worker lease. Cancellation, ownership loss, replaced leases and expiry prevent publication. Retries use a fresh attempt object under exports/jobs/workspace/{workspace}/{job}/; results and signatures never outlive the job's 24 hours from request. Startup/pump/shutdown use EXPORTS_ENABLED, still off by default, with the existing private S3 configuration and job lifecycle.

Ready email has a separate leased outbox in the job. Storage completion remains available if mail fails; transport retries do not regenerate the ZIP. Sending requires the requester to remain the current owner and have a current verified auth-account email. Revoked ownership suppresses delivery. Localized en/pt/es HTML/text uses the shared mail layout and a stable provider idempotency key. The email points to an authenticated workspace export page, so forwarding an email does not give a download capability. Current-owner access and expiry are checked again before signing the file. Configure APP_URL, RESEND_API_KEY, MAIL_FROM and the intended MAIL_ALLOWLIST; absent/unavailable mail transport leaves a retryable pending notification. The ready link opens the authenticated job page; signing in preserves the exact validated workspace-export destination. Incoming headers cannot supply an alternate return path.

apps/worker/src/workspace-exports.integration.test.ts verifies a 5,001-link ZIP, a 2,501-link legacy bio, all content categories, one cross-file snapshot during writes, secret/tenant isolation, all stored aggregates on a free plan, owner changes, concurrent active requests/expiry, running cancellation, retries and stale leases, separate mail retry/idempotency and a real BullMQ pump. apps/web/e2e/workspace-exports-http.local.ts verifies actual session HTTP and an 18-entry private S3 ZIP, metadata bounds, free-owner access, current-role refusal, kind/tenant isolation, UUIDs, cancellation/history/expiry. Evidence is in .impeccable/review/p6-workspace-export-backend/http-evidence.json.

Workspace dashboard

The current owner sees Export workspace in General settings. The in-page review at /{workspace}/settings/workspace/export explains archive scope, exclusions, the 1 GiB limit, one-active-job limit and 24-hour expiry. A live job replaces Prepare with Continue export. Submission uses a stable request UUID and a local duplicate guard; no library rows are fetched into the browser.

/{workspace}/settings/workspace/exports/{id} shows truthful phase/row progress, cancellation, expiry, private ZIP download and separate pending/sent/failed email state. Polling pauses in hidden tabs and continues at a lower frequency for a completed archive whose email is pending. A completed download remains available while email retries; expired or unauthorized reads remove it. Manual actions invalidate stale poll responses. History at .../exports uses shared filters, divided list rows and server-side 25-row pagination.

apps/web/e2e/workspace-exports-ui.local.ts verifies an isolated free workspace with 5,001 links, 100 tags and 2,501 legacy bio references, real BullMQ/private synthetic S3 generation and download of all 18 ZIP entries, duplicate submission, active-job continuation, cancellation, history pages/state filtering, retry, owner loss and expiry. A fake notifier verifies pending-to-sent polling and the signed-out email → sign-in → exact job → ZIP flow without real provider mail. Desktop/mobile en/pt/es light/dark evidence and design review live in .impeccable/review/p6-workspace-export-ui/. Helper tests reject external, traversing and malformed return paths. Real email/R2/staging acceptance and remaining P6 requirements stay open.

getting-started.title: Getting started with the Shortn API
getting-started.markdown:
# Getting started with the Shortn API

Shortn manages short links, QR codes, campaigns, tags, bio pages and domains in a workspace.
The API is being rolled out behind workspace feature flags. An API key does not enable access to a disabled feature.

## Authentication

Create a key in **Settings → API keys**. Only workspace owners and admins can manage keys.
Copy the secret when it is created; it is shown once. Give each integration the scopes it needs.
The key's permissions are intersected with its creator's current workspace role.
Revocation, membership removal and role changes apply to subsequent requests.

Send `Authorization: Bearer sk_live_…` over HTTPS to `https://api.shortn.at`.
Session cookies do not authenticate REST requests. Never put secrets in URLs or client-side code.

```sh
curl https://api.shortn.at/v1/workspace \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SHORTN_API_KEY"
```

## Create a link

Use a key with `links:write`. Keep the same `Idempotency-Key` when retrying a POST.
Use a new key for a different operation. A reused key with a different payload is rejected.

```sh
curl https://api.shortn.at/v1/links \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SHORTN_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Idempotency-Key: my-integration-create-001' \
  --data '{"url":"https://example.com","title":"Example"}'
```

## Pagination and filters

List endpoints return bounded pages. Use the returned `nextCursor` as the next request's
`cursor`, preserving the other filters. A missing next cursor ends the list.
The reference documents each endpoint's supported `limit`, search and filter parameters.
For a large link library, use tag and campaign filters alongside keyword search;
keep selections by stable link ID across pages. Do not download the whole library to populate a picker.

## Expand related metadata

Link lists and all link lookup routes accept `?expand=tags,campaign`.
Each link keeps its compact `tags` and `utm` fields. Optional full records appear
in `expanded.tags` and `expanded.campaign`. Both are arrays: a link can have
multiple tags and campaigns, and repeated references are returned once.

Requesting tags requires `tags:read`; campaigns requires `campaigns:read`, in
addition to `links:read`. A missing scope returns 403. Unknown expansion names
return 400. Omit `expand` to keep the compact response and avoid the related reads.
Expansion joins only the requested page (at most 200 links), with workspace
isolation and legacy reference support. Deleted, merged without a surviving
alias, or foreign-workspace references are omitted. Campaign link counts are
computed without returning the campaign's full link ID list.

```sh
curl 'https://api.shortn.at/v1/links?limit=50&expand=tags,campaign' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SHORTN_API_KEY"
```

## Errors and retries

Errors use `application/problem+json` with a stable `code`. Dates are ISO strings and IDs are strings.
Check HTTP status and `code`; do not parse human-readable error text.
Rate limits apply per key and expose `RateLimit-*` headers. On a 429, respect `Retry-After`.
Retry transient failures with backoff, preserving the idempotency key for POST requests.
Feature, role and scope failures require configuration changes rather than repeated retries.

See the [API reference](/docs/api), its [markdown version](/docs/api.md),
and the [webhook guide](/docs/webhooks).

imports.title: CSV imports
imports.markdown:
# CSV imports

The link and QR import backend and dashboard are implemented locally and disabled by default. A local filtered-CSV round trip through the actual import worker is verified; the in-page filtered export UI is also implemented locally; external acceptance remains open. There are no public import REST routes yet.

## Worker configuration

Set `IMPORTS_ENABLED=1` on the web app and worker only after provisioning private storage and
job indexes. Enabled startup requires `S3_ENDPOINT`, `S3_REGION`, `S3_BUCKET`,
`S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`; production storage must use HTTPS.
Run `bun run db:indexes` and use the existing durable Redis configuration. The
worker discovers bounded pages of Mongo-backed jobs into BullMQ and recovers
expired leases after a restart. The flag defaults to `0`.

Input objects under `imports/{workspaceId}/{importId}.csv` must remain private.
Presigned PUT grants expire in 15 minutes and sign the exact length, CSV type,
private cache control and conditional no-overwrite header. The provider must
accept these headers through browser CORS. The real bucket's signing, conditional
PUT and lifecycle behavior still needs staging acceptance. Error CSV output under
`exports/jobs/imports/` requires a 24-hour lifecycle and private signed delivery.

## Pipeline

Core creates an actor/workspace-bound link or QR upload job with a 24-hour lifetime. Inspection
reads at most 10 MiB in the worker, parses at most 50,000 rows and snapshots source
rows in 500-row transactions. A SHA-256 source hash prevents mixed snapshots after
an upload changes during recovery. Poll views contain column names, row count and
only the first 20 rows, with preview cells bounded to 200 characters.

Mapping supports destination (`url`, `destination`, `long_url`), key (`key`, `slug`,
`code`), title, tags, UTM fields, expiry and domain. Ambiguous headers need an
explicit choice. A mapping change creates a new result generation; it cannot
change an import that is already committing.

Dry runs validate every row through the same URL, key, reserved-name, domain and
plan-feature checks as ordinary link creation. They detect duplicate custom keys
within the file, retain row-specific failures and stream a formula-safe error CSV.
No links, tags or quota reservations are created by a dry run. The ready summary
shows valid/error counts by code and advisory quota availability; commit rechecks
capacity before writing.

Commit reserves link or QR capacity for the whole valid set before any imported resource is
created. A refusal reports exact used, reserved, requested and available numbers.
Other v2 creates and imports respect this hold. Commits create at most 500 rows per
transaction through the shared creation pipeline. Link/tag writes, safety metadata,
mutation events, capacity consumption, row identities, receipt and job checkpoint
commit together. QR imports also insert the QR document and hidden backing link
in that transaction, with the standard default design. They charge QR quota and
preserve mapped keys, custom domains, destination/UTM, title, tags and expiry.
Retried chunks return stable resource IDs without duplicating either document.

Each committed receipt is invalidated again and warmed through the redirect
service's shared loader and generation-aware Redis cache, with at most 16 parallel
loads. A separate warming checkpoint resumes work after a post-commit cache
failure. Cache fills retain their normal fail-open behavior during outages;
required invalidation errors remain retryable. QR scan
identity is resolved by backing-link ID and legacy public-ID fallback, so identical
keys on different domains cannot select another QR's scan identity.

Lease checks occur inside the chunk transaction. Cancellation releases only
remaining capacity; an obsolete lease cannot write more rows. The worker checks
the creator's current membership and creation permission during every stage and
before each chunk. Terminal infrastructure failures release remaining holds.
Committed rows remain counted as usage. A commit whose rows are all created
finishes its completion event rather than accepting a late cancellation.

`import.completed` and the completed job state share a transaction. A failed
outbox write retries completion without recreating links. Only import identifiers
and counts enter the completion payload. Status and error delivery recheck current
workspace access, and signatures cannot outlive the job.

## Legacy coexistence

Deploy the updated legacy application and v2 writer code before enabling imports
while both applications accept creates. They share a stable legacy-identity lock
and the workspace mutation lock, including a legacy create that begins before a
personal workspace is provisioned. The legacy adapter uses its own Mongoose
connection/session; it does not mix BSON values or sessions from another driver.

Accepting an import sets an internal workspace marker that makes document-based
v2 quota authoritative for subsequent legacy link and QR creates. This continues
after the hold is consumed, released or expires, so legacy meter lag cannot admit
writes beyond the period limit. Legacy plan checks remain in place; accounts that
have never accepted an import retain their earlier behavior. Held capacity stays
separate for links and QRs, and refusals preserve the existing `plan-limit` result
with exact quota details.

The two legacy writes that create a QR/backing pair now share the quota transaction.
A failed QR write cannot leave an orphan backing link. Title/tag reads, password
hashing, cache invalidation and usage delivery stay outside the transaction.

## Verification and remaining gates

Local tests use real Mongo transactions, cache Redis and durable BullMQ with
synthetic private storage. They cover dry runs/errors, mapping generations,
whole-import quota refusal, cancellation, permission loss, changed input and
completion-event retries. A child worker is killed after 500 of 1,001 rows commit;
a replacement completes the job with exactly 1,001 rows and three receipts. The
same process-kill test covers QR imports and verifies 1,001 complete QR/backing
pairs, unique link references and QR-only usage. Rollback tests reject a QR insert
after backing rows are staged and verify that rows, tags, receipt, capacity and
checkpoint all roll back. Custom-domain tests cover view/design/export data,
cached scan identity, edit/delete and a same-key record on another domain.

A complete 50,000-link local run (inspection, dry run and commit) finished in
38.6 seconds with cache warming and synthetic private storage. This does not satisfy
the required staging acceptance. Real bucket CORS/conditional PUT/lifecycle and staging rollout remain
open. The full P6 goal is still active.

## Dashboard

Links and QR library headers open `/{workspace}/imports/new?kind=links|qr`.
The in-page form uploads CSV bytes directly to a private signed PUT; server
actions accept only byte count and resource kind. Pasted URLs are converted to
the same CSV format in the browser. Upload progress, cancellation and errors stay
in the form. Signing failures remove the unused upload job, and upload-completion
retries reuse the existing job.

`/{workspace}/imports/{id}` provides column mapping, the bounded 20-row preview,
full dry-run review, private error CSV download, exact quota numbers, explicit
creation of all valid rows, cancellation and background progress. After a dry
run, mapping and source preview are expandable so row results remain easy to
reach. Polling only runs during active phases while the tab is visible. An expiry
refresh removes the job and signed attachment after its lifetime.

History at `/{workspace}/imports` and row results both paginate on the server at
25 per page. Members/viewers see their own jobs; owners/admins may inspect other
workspace jobs. Only the creator with current create permission can upload,
remap or commit. Cancellation uses current resource-delete permission. Every
server action authenticates workspace access again. Row filters support literal
keyword search, server-searched tags, valid/invalid state, specific errors and
grouping by error. Tag suggestions are capped at 50; row labels and source column
names are bounded. Storage keys, worker leases, source cells and full result
sets are excluded from dashboard responses.

The web flag defaults to `0`, independently of `QR_EXPORTS_ENABLED`. Enabled web
startup requires all five private S3 settings and HTTPS in production. Deploy the
new indexes before enabling. English, Portuguese and Spanish use the existing
Page, FilterBar, list and Pagination controls; all flows are in-page.

Run the synthetic local browser harness against the P6 sandbox:

```sh
bun --no-env-file apps/web/e2e/imports.local.ts
```

It owns loopback private storage and a real BullMQ import worker, checks actual
conditional browser PUT headers, CSV and pasted URL input, mapping-error recovery,
dry runs without creation, error CSV download, row/history pagination, tags,
quota refusal, cancellation, and successful link/QR creation. Captures and
assertion evidence live in `.impeccable/review/p6-import-ui/`. A separate Mongo
integration check verifies bounded 25-row responses for a 50,000-row result set,
actor/workspace isolation, expiry, literal searches, tag caps and upload retries.
These checks do not establish real-provider or staging acceptance.

## Shortn export round trips

Shortn CSV exports declare `shortn_format=shortn-csv-v1` on every row. Values that
could become spreadsheet formulas receive a leading apostrophe; literal leading
apostrophes are doubled. The importer removes that protection only for declared
Shortn rows. Tags in this format are a JSON array inside the quoted CSV cell,
so commas, semicolons, quotes, Unicode and apostrophes inside tag names survive.
Unknown/blank declared versions and malformed tag arrays are rejected. Ordinary
third-party CSV keeps its existing delimiter-based tags and literal values.

Destinations retain their complete query and fragment, including repeated UTM
parameters; export does not split/rewrite them into separate UTM columns. A local
integration test exports a filtered source workspace, frees its global key, and
imports the CSV into a different workspace through inspection, dry run and commit.
It verifies destination, available key, tags, title, UTM and expiry. Existing
10 MiB/50,000-row import limits still apply to exported files being re-imported.

Legacy plan checks remain in place; accounts that have never accepted an import retain their earlier behavior. Held capacity stays separate for links and QRs, and refusals preserve the existing plan-limit result with exact quota details.

The two legacy writes that create a QR/backing pair now share the quota transaction. A failed QR write cannot leave an orphan backing link. Title/tag reads, password hashing, cache invalidation and usage delivery stay outside the transaction.

Verification and remaining gates

Local tests use real Mongo transactions, cache Redis and durable BullMQ with synthetic private storage. They cover dry runs/errors, mapping generations, whole-import quota refusal, cancellation, permission loss, changed input and completion-event retries. A child worker is killed after 500 of 1,001 rows commit; a replacement completes the job with exactly 1,001 rows and three receipts. The same process-kill test covers QR imports and verifies 1,001 complete QR/backing pairs, unique link references and QR-only usage. Rollback tests reject a QR insert after backing rows are staged and verify that rows, tags, receipt, capacity and checkpoint all roll back. Custom-domain tests cover view/design/export data, cached scan identity, edit/delete and a same-key record on another domain.

A complete 50,000-link local run (inspection, dry run and commit) finished in 38.6 seconds with cache warming and synthetic private storage. This does not satisfy the required staging acceptance. Real bucket CORS/conditional PUT/lifecycle and staging rollout remain open. The full P6 goal is still active.

Dashboard

Links and QR library headers open /{workspace}/imports/new?kind=links|qr. The in-page form uploads CSV bytes directly to a private signed PUT; server actions accept only byte count and resource kind. Pasted URLs are converted to the same CSV format in the browser. Upload progress, cancellation and errors stay in the form. Signing failures remove the unused upload job, and upload-completion retries reuse the existing job.

/{workspace}/imports/{id} provides column mapping, the bounded 20-row preview, full dry-run review, private error CSV download, exact quota numbers, explicit creation of all valid rows, cancellation and background progress. After a dry run, mapping and source preview are expandable so row results remain easy to reach. Polling only runs during active phases while the tab is visible. An expiry refresh removes the job and signed attachment after its lifetime.

History at /{workspace}/imports and row results both paginate on the server at 25 per page. Members/viewers see their own jobs; owners/admins may inspect other workspace jobs. Only the creator with current create permission can upload, remap or commit. Cancellation uses current resource-delete permission. Every server action authenticates workspace access again. Row filters support literal keyword search, server-searched tags, valid/invalid state, specific errors and grouping by error. Tag suggestions are capped at 50; row labels and source column names are bounded. Storage keys, worker leases, source cells and full result sets are excluded from dashboard responses.

The web flag defaults to 0, independently of QR_EXPORTS_ENABLED. Enabled web startup requires all five private S3 settings and HTTPS in production. Deploy the new indexes before enabling. English, Portuguese and Spanish use the existing Page, FilterBar, list and Pagination controls; all flows are in-page.

Run the synthetic local browser harness against the P6 sandbox:

bun --no-env-file apps/web/e2e/imports.local.ts

It owns loopback private storage and a real BullMQ import worker, checks actual conditional browser PUT headers, CSV and pasted URL input, mapping-error recovery, dry runs without creation, error CSV download, row/history pagination, tags, quota refusal, cancellation, and successful link/QR creation. Captures and assertion evidence live in .impeccable/review/p6-import-ui/. A separate Mongo integration check verifies bounded 25-row responses for a 50,000-row result set, actor/workspace isolation, expiry, literal searches, tag caps and upload retries. These checks do not establish real-provider or staging acceptance.

Shortn export round trips

Shortn CSV exports declare shortn_format=shortn-csv-v1 on every row. Values that could become spreadsheet formulas receive a leading apostrophe; literal leading apostrophes are doubled. The importer removes that protection only for declared Shortn rows. Tags in this format are a JSON array inside the quoted CSV cell, so commas, semicolons, quotes, Unicode and apostrophes inside tag names survive. Unknown/blank declared versions and malformed tag arrays are rejected. Ordinary third-party CSV keeps its existing delimiter-based tags and literal values.

Destinations retain their complete query and fragment, including repeated UTM parameters; export does not split/rewrite them into separate UTM columns. A local integration test exports a filtered source workspace, frees its global key, and imports the CSV into a different workspace through inspection, dry run and commit. It verifies destination, available key, tags, title, UTM and expiry. Existing 10 MiB/50,000-row import limits still apply to exported files being re-imported.

link-rules.markdown:
# Link rules

Link creation, bulk creation and editing accept a `rules` object. Link reads return
configured rules with UTC ISO timestamps. `PATCH /v1/links/{id}` replaces the whole
rules object when `rules` is supplied; send `rules: null` to clear it. Omit the
field to preserve existing rules. Link write scopes and current workspace roles apply.

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "activeFrom": "2026-11-01T08:00:00.000Z",
    "expiresAt": "2026-12-01T08:00:00.000Z",
    "expiredUrl": "https://example.com/campaign-ended",
    "maxClicks": 10000,
    "forwardQuery": true,
    "utm": { "source": "newsletter", "campaign": "November" },
    "permanent": false
  }
}
```

## Schedule and expiry

Activation is inclusive: the link starts redirecting at `activeFrom`. Expiry is
exclusive: at `expiresAt` it stops redirecting to its destination. When both are
present, activation must precede expiry. The redirect checks these timestamps
on every request, including a cache hit.

Rule mutations also persist versioned invalidation requests. The worker uses
BullMQ delayed jobs to evict canonical and alias cache entries at activation and
expiry boundaries. Edited or cleared rules supersede older jobs. Requests remain
in Mongo until invalidation succeeds, so queue publication and cache failures can
be retried. Timestamp checks remain authoritative during worker or Redis outages.

Safety and password checks run first. Without a fallback, scheduled links return
a branded 404 page and expired links return a branded 410 page in the visitor's
language. With `expiredUrl`, either time gate returns a 302 to that URL. Gate and
fallback responses do not count as destination clicks. Query forwarding, fixed
UTM and permanent redirect settings do not apply to the fallback.

Fallbacks must be public HTTP(S) destinations and pass the same structural
validation as a link destination. Safety scans include the fallback and keep the
highest risk verdict. Changing a fallback marks safety pending, preserves existing
blocks, and prevents a scan for the previous fallback from applying afterward.

## Approximate visit limit

`maxClicks` accepts an integer from zero through 9,007,199,254,740,991. It limits
lifetime non-bot destination visits, including QR scans and persisted visits from
before the limit was configured. Zero closes the link immediately. Safety, password and
time gates run before the count check; targeting and rotation run afterward.

The redirect reads a durable Redis hot counter seeded from persisted click and
scan totals. Tracked human visits increment it with the analytics stream write;
bots and gate responses do not increment it. Legacy QR links without an analytics
record still count allowed human visits. Counters have no idle expiry, including
when no analytics record exists to seed them again. After counter loss, tracked
links seed from their latest persisted totals. Untracked legacy QR visits from
before counting began, or lost counters without persisted history, cannot be
reconstructed.

This is an approximate limit: concurrent requests, queued analytics writes,
spool replay and persistence lag can overshoot it. Label it “about” in interfaces.
It does not count unique visitors. A missing counter service returns a retryable
503 for a limited destination rather than bypassing the limit. Existing safety,
password and time gates remain usable without that service.

At the limit, visitors receive a localized branded 410 page, or a 302 to
`expiredUrl` when configured. That fallback does not count, forward query
parameters, apply UTM settings or set a rotation cookie. Permanent redirects can
be cached by clients and bypass future server checks; use the default 302 for
links whose visit limit needs to be checked on returning visits.

## Query forwarding and UTM

`forwardQuery` defaults to false. When true, incoming parameters are appended to
the destination, with these rules:

- Existing destination parameters take precedence over incoming values.
- Repeated incoming values are preserved when the destination has no such key.
- `token`, `q`, `ref` and `block` are reserved for Shortn and are not forwarded.
- At most 50 parameters are appended, with keys capped at 100 characters and
  values at 500 characters.
- Fixed `utm.source`, `medium`, `campaign`, `term` and `content` overwrite both
  destination and incoming UTM values. Each configured value is capped at 200
  characters. Empty values do not add a parameter.

Destination fragments are preserved. Click events record the effective UTM
values applied to the redirect while retaining the existing attribution flow.

## App deep links

`deepLink` selects an app link for matching iOS or Android user agents, after
safety, password, time and visit-limit gates and before device/country targeting
or rotation:

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "deepLink": {
      "ios": "youtube://watch?v=123",
      "android": "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=123",
      "fallback": "store",
      "store": {
        "ios": "https://apps.apple.com/app/youtube/id544007664",
        "android": "https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.google.android.youtube"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Configure at least one OS target. App links accept public HTTPS URLs or these
app schemes: `youtube`, `spotify`, `whatsapp`, `tg`, `instagram`, `fb`, `twitter`,
`linkedin`, `slack`, `discord`, `zoomus`. Other handlers, executable schemes,
credentials, whitespace and control characters are rejected. App and store URLs
are capped at 2,048 characters. Public HTTPS app links and store URLs participate
in safety scans; custom app schemes cannot be inspected by HTTP safety providers.

`fallback: "web"` uses the link's main destination. `fallback: "store"` requires
an explicit HTTPS store URL for every configured OS, under `apps.apple.com` for
iOS and `play.google.com` for Android. It never guesses a store listing. Unknown
OS values and recognized bots continue through the ordinary targeting rules.

A matching visit returns a localized, private, non-cacheable HTML handoff with
an automatic app-open attempt and visible app/fallback links. If the page remains
visible, it navigates to the fallback after about 1.8 seconds. Becoming hidden,
losing focus or leaving the page cancels that timer; returning does not start it
again. The app button retries and starts a new timer. Without JavaScript both
links remain usable. Browsers may require a tap or confirmation before opening
an app; an installed app cannot be reliably detected from the web page. HTTPS
universal/app links navigate directly and use the OS/browser's handling.

Query forwarding and fixed UTM apply to the app and fallback URL. A handoff
records one click/scan with `m.branch` of `deep:ios` or `deep:android`; this measures
the handoff attempt, not confirmed app installation or launch. Browser fallback
and retry controls do not create extra Shortn events. Deep handoffs do not set a
rotation cookie or use a permanent redirect, regardless of `permanent`.

## Device and country targeting

Configure up to ten ordered `device` rules and ten ordered `geo` rules:

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "device": [
      { "os": "ios", "device": "mobile", "url": "https://example.com/ios" },
      { "device": "mobile", "url": "https://example.com/mobile" }
    ],
    "geo": [
      { "country": "PT", "url": "https://example.com/portugal" },
      { "country": "ES", "url": "https://example.com/spain" }
    ]
  }
}
```

Safety, password and time gates run before targeting. The first matching device
rule wins; if none matches, the first matching country rule wins. Otherwise the
link's main destination is used. An OS and device in the same rule must both
match. Each device rule must specify at least one of them. Supported OS values
are `ios`, `android`, `windows`, `macos`; devices are `mobile`, `tablet`, `desktop`.
Device/OS comes from the request user agent and country from the trusted
Cloudflare `CF-IPCountry` header. Country rules use uppercase two-letter codes.
Unknown OS/country values do not match those predicates.

Every target URL must pass public HTTP(S) structural validation. All configured
targets are included in safety scans, even when they are not selected for the
current visitor. Editing the destination set queues a new scan and supersedes
older scans. Query forwarding, fixed UTM and permanent redirect behavior apply
to the selected destination.

## Weighted rotation

A `rotation` list selects among one to ten public HTTP(S) destinations after
all gates and device/country rules:

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "rotation": [
      { "url": "https://example.com/a", "weight": 1 },
      { "url": "https://example.com/b", "weight": 3 }
    ]
  }
}
```

Weights are relative: this example assigns about one quarter of fresh selections
to A and three quarters to B. Each weight must be positive, finite and no greater
than 1,000,000. All rotation URLs are structurally validated and included in safety
scans. Changing only weights does not require rescanning the same destinations.

The first selection sets a host-only `_sr_{linkId}` cookie for one hour, with
`Secure`, `HttpOnly` and `SameSite=Lax`. It stores a configuration fingerprint and
option number rather than a visitor identifier. Subsequent visits reuse that
option without refreshing expiry. Changing URLs, option order or weights
invalidates the previous fingerprint and selects again. Malformed or out-of-range
cookie values are ignored. Without cookies, each request gets a fresh selection.

Device/country matches and safety/password/time gates do not create a rotation
cookie. Query forwarding, fixed UTM and permanent redirect settings apply to the
selected option. Use the default 302 when rotation changes should reach returning
visitors promptly; clients may remember permanent redirects.

## Branch analytics

Targeted destination clicks carry `m.branch`: `device:0`, `geo:0`, `rotation:0`, and so on,
or `destination` when no targeting rule matched. Numbers are zero-based rule
positions; editing or reordering rules changes what a position represents.
Links without targeting retain the existing event format, with no branch field.

The REST analytics endpoints accept `groupBy=branch` and `branch=geo:0` filters,
subject to the existing analytics-breakdown plan gate and workspace isolation.
The click pipeline preserves branch values during retries, and daily rollups
include `byBranch`. Safety/password/time gates produce no destination click.
The dashboard branch breakdown view remains part of the advanced management UI
work; the REST breakdown is available now.

## Permanent redirects

`permanent: true` uses HTTP 301 for the final destination hop. The default remains
HTTP 302. Destination clicks are still enqueued, and the server sends
`Cache-Control: private, max-age=0`. Permanent redirects can be remembered by
clients; prefer the default for links whose destination or rules may change.

## Social preview overrides

Link creation, bulk creation and editing accept a top-level `og` object:

```json
{
  "url": "https://example.com/article",
  "og": {
    "title": "The article title",
    "description": "A short description for a shared link.",
    "image": "https://images.example.com/article-card.png"
  }
}
```

Configure at least one field. Titles are capped at 200 characters, descriptions
at 500, and image URLs at 2,048. Empty fields and unknown keys are rejected. Images
must use public HTTPS URLs without credentials. Shortn does not fetch or upload
these images in the redirect path; social platforms fetch the configured URL.
Use a stable image URL accessible without authentication.

`PATCH /v1/links/{id}` replaces the whole `og` object when supplied. Send
`og: null` to clear it; omit it to preserve existing metadata. Reads return the
configured object. Creation and bulk creation share the same validation. Metadata
mutations invalidate canonical and historical-alias cache entries.

Recognized preview UAs include `facebookexternalhit`, `Facebot`, `Twitterbot`,
`LinkedInBot`, `Slackbot-LinkExpanding`, `Discordbot`, `TelegramBot`, `WhatsApp`,
`SkypeUriPreview`, `MicrosoftPreview`, `Pinterestbot` and `redditbot`. Matching is
case-insensitive and examines at most 2,000 characters. This is response selection,
not crawler authentication; user-agent strings can be copied. Search crawlers and
other automated clients retain normal redirects.

After safety, password, time and visit-limit gates, a preview bot gets private HTML
with escaped Open Graph/Twitter metadata and a meta refresh to the selected web
destination. The canonical `og:url` is the short URL without request query values.
An omitted preview title falls back to the link's title. An omitted image does
not invent an image URL. Device/country/rotation selection and query/UTM rules
still apply, but preview responses do not set rotation cookies or open native
apps. Humans keep normal redirect or deep-link behavior.

Recorded preview requests remain marked as bots in the click stream. They contribute
to bot volume rather than human click/scan analytics, click webhooks or the hot
visit count. Gate and fallback responses do not expose configured preview
metadata. Responses vary by user agent and are private with zero freshness;
platforms may keep their own preview cache and may require a fresh scrape after
an edit. The advanced in-page preview editor remains pending.

## Destination health

Link reads include read-only `health` results when a current check is scheduled.
`health.checks` contains individual destination results; `checkedAt` is the last
completed cycle and `nextCheckAt` is the next queued check time. An empty checks
list means the first check is pending. Queued checks may run after their due time
while a backlog drains.

The worker checks the main destination and configured web targets, including
fallback, device/country/rotation URLs, HTTPS app links and store URLs. Custom
app schemes are excluded. URLs differing only by fragment share a check. A cycle
runs weekly, with one target checked per job and bounded batches for large
libraries. Requests are limited per hostname across worker instances.

Checks use HEAD, falling back to GET with a one-byte Range request for HTTP 405
or 501. The connection closes after response headers, even if a server ignores
Range. Up to three redirects are followed, with public-address validation and
DNS pinning on every hop. Private, mixed public/private DNS and credential-bearing
targets are not requested. Redirect loops, DNS/network failures and timeouts
produce an unknown/unreachable result, not an assumed HTTP error.

Each check reports `status` (`ok`, `http_error`, `unreachable`, `blocked`), optional
HTTP status, check time, consecutive HTTP-error `streak`, and `failingSince`.
`health.flagged` becomes true after two consecutive 4xx/5xx checks of any target.
A healthy response clears that target's streak. Network/blocked outcomes do not
pretend that the page returned a 4xx/5xx status. Failure codes exclude remote
response bodies and credentials.

Health is informational: results never disable a link, change safety status or
modify its redirect. Websites may treat the checker differently from a browser.
The checker identifies itself as `Shortn-LinkHealth/1.0`, and Shortn treats its
requests as bots so checks of other Shortn links do not inflate human analytics.
Changing the destination set resets the check generation and hides old results;
late results cannot apply to an edited link. Metadata-only edits retain results.

The same workspace permissions and link-read API scopes apply. Health fields
cannot be written through link mutations. Active dashboard rows flag repeated
HTTP errors and open the link overview's Destination health section. It shows
per-target status and check dates, distinguishes blocked and unreachable results,
and hides stale results after a destination edit. Health remains informational.

Dashboard Links and QR selections persist across pages and filters, up to 500
items per action. Delete opens the existing permission-checked review page.
This dashboard limit is separate from the REST bulk-create limit of 1,000.

## Remaining rule features

Unsupported rule fields are rejected. The advanced
in-page rule editor also remains pending. Background safety scans for new or
changed link destinations are durable: the worker executes them through BullMQ,
retries failures with bounded exponential backoff, and rescans successful links
weekly. A destination edit supersedes any older queued or running request.
`WEB_RISK_API_KEY` must be configured in the worker for Google Web Risk checks;
without it the existing structural/domain-age checks still run. A configured
reputation-provider outage is retried rather than treated as a completed weekly scan.

Safety-provider results use shared Redis caching. RDAP registration timestamps
are cached per destination host for 24 hours; domain age is recalculated for
each scan. Web Risk threat matches remain specific to the exact URL and expire
at the provider's `expireTime`, following the
[Lookup API cache protocol](https://docs.cloud.google.com/web-risk/docs/caching).
Clean Lookup responses and provider failures are not cached. A clean path does
not establish trust for other URLs on that host. Cache outages fall through to
provider checks, and configured reputation outages retain durable retries.
